claims.text: Coating tungsten powders with a thin, conformal copper layer by vapor deposition before consolidation improves W–Cu interfacial contact.
The copper coating improves interfacial contact by reducing the surface-energy mismatch between W and Cu.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact limits void formation during sintering.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact limits phase separation during sintering.
Reduced void formation and phase separation enhance thermal transport.
Reduced void formation and phase separation enhance mechanical durability under irradiation.
W–Cu materials produced by spark-plasma sintering or mechanical alloying typically exhibit interfacial voids and phase-separation defects.
A pre-deposited copper layer can produce improved, near-perfect bonding between copper and tungsten.
The pre-deposited copper layer effectively eliminates interfacial voids.
Vapor-deposited copper promotes superior wettability during W–Cu sintering.
Vapor-deposited copper suppresses phase separation during W–Cu sintering.
Improved W–Cu interfacial structure better accommodates thermal stresses.
Improved W–Cu interfacial structure better accommodates irradiation-induced stresses.
Relative to an otherwise comparable uncoated composite, the vapor-coated composite will have fewer interfacial voids.
Relative to an otherwise comparable uncoated composite, the vapor-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to an otherwise comparable uncoated composite, the vapor-coated composite will have improved mechanical durability under irradiation.
Deposition uniformity and sintering dynamics under irradiation conditions will affect the magnitude of the thermal and mechanical improvements.
